div.div: بَيْذَقٌ [meaning A pawn] in the game of chess is from ↓ بَيَاذَقَةٌ ; (TA;) which latter signifies footmen, as opposed to horsemen, (AO, K, TA,) and is an arabicized word, from the Persian, (AO, TA,) originally پِيَادَهْ: (TA:) the pl. of بيذق is بَيَاذِقُ; for which a poet uses بُذُوقٌ, as though he suppressed the ى [in the sing.], making بيذق to become ↓ بَذْقٌ : (Ibn-Buzurj, TA:) or, accord. to El-Khárzenjee, (JK, TA,) ↓ بَذْقٌ signifies a guide in a journey; as also بَيْذَقٌ: (JK, K, TA:) or [in the CK “and”] small and light or active: (K, TA:) or, as in the Tekmileh, (TA,) short and light or active: (JK, TA:) and its pl. is بُذُوقْ. (JK, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
